Longmire is a pretty great show. Not too impressed so far with the newest season though. You mentioned you got the round barrel for the sights. Did the octagon barrel not come with sights on it or were they in a style you didnt like?

Glad you like it. My first real .22 was a Winchester 9422 lever gun that was very much like yours, and I put many thousands of rounds through it.

The tube loading is much faster than gate loading for a .22 - you can pick up and insert three or four cartridges at a time once you get the hang of it, just line them up and slide them in like they were on a stripper clip. I was taught to put the butt plate on top of my foot, and to allow the rifle to tip backwards about 20 degrees from vertical. This made loading a little easier and kept the muzzle safely away from my body.

Many folks these days - even target shooters - do not clean .22 rimfire rifle barrels, they just push one oily patch through after a shooting session and call it good. This is heresy to some, but cleaning causes significant wear and tear, and low-pressure, outside lubricated .22s are essentially harmless to steel and your bore will last forever if that's all that touches it. This means that a worn .22 barrel is a barrel that has been worn by cleaning, not shooting. That one oily patch is just to protect against rust. You can scrub your barrel clean after every range trip, but why? After three shots its fouled again and remains that way for the rest of the session. Clean the bore once, very well, when you take it out of the box and just oil it lightly thereafter. You'll still want to clean the rest of the mechanism of course.

Lever guns are at their best with open sights - try it against moving targets, such as a can on a string, or a swinging plate. If you do want to mount the scope, try a little blue locktite in between the mounts and the groove.

I bought a Henry Golden Boy in .22 for my sister when she turned 16. The rimfire lever guns from Henry are all really nice from what I've been able to tell. Accurate and reliable. The only downside is how long they can take to reload, but other than that I really like them.
